reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses deformation behavior and elemental effects in completely different refractory BCC high-entropy alloys (NbTaTiV, HfMoNbTaTiZr) and provides no information on SiC precipitation, crack-blunting mechanisms, or caloric phase transitions in (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38. Therefore, none of the key premises are supported by the provided passages.
premises: Si and C additions will form in-situ nanoscale SiC precipitates in the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 matrix.
SiC precipitates will act as crack-blunting reinforcements and improve load transfer, enhancing fracture toughness.
The caloric phase transition (order-disorder) will remain essentially undisturbed by the SiC precipitates.
The reinforced alloy will show significantly improved load-bearing integrity (e.g., fracture toughness, tensile strength).
The caloric performance (entropy change) will remain nearly unchanged compared to the unreinforced alloy.
